description: The shared Plexus update-bot preset (§ 2 PLX-Updates); every Plexus repo extends it with one line.

Third-party patch, minor and digest updates from every manager arrive once a week in one pull request, merged on green CI; lock file maintenance arrives the same morning in a pull request of its own, merged the same way. Majors, third-party 0.x minors, prereleases and security fixes come one by one; all but the security fixes wait for a human.

One writer per pin (§ 1 PLX-Updates): the release train writes the plexus-ms/primitives workflow refs and collection pin, the plx pin in mise.toml and the exact @plexus-ms/config pin, so the bot leaves them alone; it proposes everything else.

A third-party release waits three days before it is proposed, security fixes included, long enough for a compromised version to be pulled; pnpm enforces the same age at install time (pnpm-workspace.yaml), so a PR never carries a version the lockfile check rejects.
The sub-presets `library` and `operations` sharpen this one for a package repo and an operations repo; the repo presets extend them.
In a package repo `plx changeset` commits the changeset a bump owes to the bot's branch (§ 5 PLX-Delivery); that author is ignored, so the branch stays the bot's to rebase.

copier.description: The hosted bot cannot run `copier update`; the release train's ship step owns template propagation.

packageRules.description: The train's pins (§ 1 PLX-Updates): the plexus-ms/primitives workflow refs and collection pin, the plx pin in mise.toml, and the exact @plexus-ms/config pin are written by `plx ship` in lockstep with the train; the bot never proposes them.
npm ranges follow the version actually tested; other managers keep their own spelling, so a floating node major in mise.toml stays floating.
@plexus-ms packages are the initiative's own, published with immutable, provenance-attested versions: no release-age wait, and patch and minor merge unattended once CI is green.

Third-party patch, minor and digest updates from every manager (npm, compose images, Dockerfile base images, tools, actions) move together once a week and merge on green CI: one pull request to review when one goes red, one deploy per week per repo. The initiative's own packages and the train's pins keep their own rules.

A third-party minor below 1.0.0 may break, as semver allows: it stays out of the weekly group and waits for a human. The regex is matched against the locked version, so it holds for ranges such as ^0.3.1.

A prerelease promises nothing, as semver allows: while an npm dependency is on one, its updates stay out of the weekly group and wait for a human. Renovate proposes a prerelease only to a dependency already on one.

The app is the unit of deployment (§ 3 PLX-Delivery): a major of one app's images moves as one PR, so one merge is one deploy and its services never run mismatched versions; patch and minor ride the weekly group. The group is named after the app directory, apps/<app>/.

A node major moves the runtime of every app in the repo at once: it waits for approval on the dependency dashboard. @types/node describes that runtime, so its major is the same decision: both wait together and move in one PR, and the types never run ahead of the node they type.

A package's `engines.node` floor states the major it supports, not the patch it was last tested on: the bump strategy would raise it on every LTS patch, so engines updates are off; the runtime itself moves with mise.toml.
A TypeScript major changes the compiler every app and package in the repo builds with: it waits for approval on the dependency dashboard.

lockFileMaintenance.description: The lock file moves within the ranges the manifests already accept, after the same three days; Renovate never groups it with other updates, so it is the second weekly pull request.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: A security fix is proposed at once, on its own, and merged on green CI, but still after the three-day release age: Renovate's default for alerts is no age at all, which pnpm would reject. In an emergency a human adds the version to minimumReleaseAgeExclude.
